title: Customer Network Commit Policy & Safeguards (PRD - WIP)
body:
Context:
- Customers want to manage networking for private deployments (VPCs/on-prem). We need an approval surface that: records intent, provides auditable proof, and keeps operators in control without blocking customer ops.
- Existing docs focus on VPC handover and attestation. This draft explores commit-style approvals (immutable receipts), bounded retry semantics, and lightweight risk scoring so audits can be concise and machine-readable.

Problem statement (short):
- When customers or operator teams make network changes that affect private deployments, current playbooks are ad-hoc: screenshots, email threads, or large blob syslogs. Hard to prove who approved what, and to roll back safely.
- Need consistent schema for approvals that supports: automated gating, human in-loop escalation, forensic bundles for post-incident review, and per-customer retention policies.

Goals:
- Design an "approval commit" primitive: small JSON receipt signed by operator + system, stored immutably and linked to telemetry.
- Define 3 approval gate presets (low/medium/high risk) with defaults and customer-overrides. Presets map to required approvers, hold times, and evidence required.
- Produce an audit-log export format suitable for legal review and fast ingestion into SIEMs (CEF/JSONL).
- Support programmatic approvals (webhooks, API tokens) and manual approvals (console button + OA-annotation).

Non-goals:
- This doc does not define cryptographic HSM integration for the commit receipts (separate KMS project).
- Not addressing full RBAC redesign — we assume existing admin roles and an operator attestation channel.

Scope (what we'll build in 1st iteration):
- Approval commit schema and storage model (immutable append-only store with trace id).
- Three gate presets and mapping to evidence checklist.
- UI/Console flow mockups for manual approval and replay.
- Exporter that emits a compressed forensic bundle (receipt + selected logs + manifest).
- Simulated import into common SIEM format for customers.

User stories / acceptance criteria:
- As a customer (network admin), I can request a change and receive a commit token that I can present to my security team. (AC: token issued with id, TTL, risk score).
- As an operator, I can approve changes via the console; the system stores a signed approval receipt and triggers configured webhooks. (AC: receipt present in audit timeline, webhook called).
- As a compliance reviewer, I can fetch a forensic bundle for a change that contains receipts, relevant syslog extracts, and hashed config diffs. (AC: bundle complete, manifest checksums match).

Approval commit primitive (proposal):
- Fields (flat list): commit_id, change_descriptor (free text short), requester (email), timestamp_utc, gate_preset, approver_ids (list), approvals: signed_signatures (strings), risk_score (0-100), evidence_refs (list of telemetry ids), ttl_seconds, commit_state (queued | approved | rejected | rolled_back), audit_hash (sha256 of canonicalized payload).
- Commits are append-only. Once approved, commit_state becomes approved and a non-mutable approved_at timestamp is recorded.
- System produces an "immutable receipt" (base64 signed blob) that customers can store off-platform for legal proof.

Gate presets (defaults):
- Low: single approver (customer-admin or operator), evidence: change descriptor + timestamp, default ttl: 30m, risk_score: 10-30. Autosucceed allowed for trusted customers with policy flag.
- Medium: two approvers (one customer, one operator), evidence: snapshot diff + CIR (connectivity impact report), ttl: 1h, risk_score: 31-70.
- High: three approvers (must include security or infra lead), evidence: snapshot diff + connectivity simulation results + pre-change rollback plan, ttl: 24h, risk_score: 71-100.

Risk scoring ideas (quick notes):
- Heuristics: number of subnets touched, exp of affected endpoints, whether change crosses AZ/region, presence of public egress rules, change to authz controls.
- Score should be tunable by customer via policy overrides (e.g., treat certain CIDR ranges as high-risk).

Audit log model and retention:
- Primary store: append-only ledger (internal). Secondary exports: per-customer compressed forensic bundles (zstd).
- Minimal export format: line-delimited JSON (JSONL) with each record containing commit_id, timestamp, actor, action, before_hash, after_hash, evidence_refs, flags.
- Retention defaults: 365 days for receipts; 90 days for attached telemetry snapshots. Allow enterprise tiers or customer policy to extend retention (legal hold).
- For privacy, we support redaction rules on export (PII scrubber plug-in).

Forensic bundle contents (proposal):
- receipt.json (immutable receipt),
- manifest.jsonl (JSONL timeline of events),
- diffs/ directory: canonicalized config diffs (hashed filenames),
- telemetry/trace_<id>.log (selected truncated logs),
- signatures.asc (operator signatures),
- README.txt (human-readable summary and chain-of-custody).

Operational considerations:
- Approval latency SLO: 99th percentile within gate TTL. Provide async fallback: if operator approval not received within TTL, route to emergency escalation policy.
- Bounded retries: if webhook delivery fails, retry with exponential backoff up to N times; include retry metadata in commit timeline.
- Storage sizing: estimate 10k commits/month for early enterprise customers, avg forensic bundle 500KB (can vary).

UX notes / console flows (rough):
- Request -> preview change -> risk score shown -> select gate/preset -> submit request -> operator console shows pending commits queue with sortable risk/age -> approve/reject/annotate -> system emits receipt and optional webhook.
- Quick-approve microflow for low-risk customers with "auto-approve" policy (requires pre-configured allowlist).

Developer APIs (surface):
- POST /v1/private/network/changes (request commit) -> returns commit_id + suggested_gate + receipt placeholder
- POST /v1/private/network/changes/{id}/approve -> body: approver_id, signature, notes
- GET /v1/private/network/changes/{id}/receipt -> returns immutable receipt (B64) or download link for forensic bundle
- GET /v1/private/network/changes?filter=... -> JSONL timeline export endpoint

Security considerations:
- Approver signatures are currently optimistic (operator-email + system signature). We should plan for future HSM/KMS signing per-tenant.
- Webhooks must be signed and include delivery receipts to avoid spoofing.
- Audit export must support customer encryption-at-rest.

Edge cases / open questions (brainstorm):
- What is the canonical "before" config? Do we snapshot entire VPC config or compute diffs from last known good? (cost tradeoff).
- How do we handle emergency changes done directly on customer infra (out-of-band) but later reconciled? Need a reconciliation flow and manual evidence ingestion.
- Should we allow operator to redact sensitive details before exporting forensic bundle? If yes, define policy & immutable audit of redactions.
- How to integrate with customers' change tickets (ServiceNow/Jira) so evidence refs are bi-directional?

Simulations & acceptance testing ideas:
- Build a small simulator to generate commits with different gate presets and validate exporter output size and SIEM ingestion.
- Run tabletop incident where a high-risk change is rolled back; verify forensic bundle gives clear timeline and approvals.

Next steps / proposed milestones (quarterly):
- Week 0-3: finalize commit schema & minimal UI mocks. Owner: Asha.
- Week 4-8: implement backend append-only store and API endpoints (proto). Owner: Eng-private-deployments.
- Week 9-12: console workflows + webhook signer + initial exporter. Owner: Console team + Observability.
- Week 13-16: pilot with 2 customers (one mid-market, one enterprise). Collect feedback and iterate.

Notes to reviewers (explicit asks):
- Please flag any policy items that would block legal/PS (retention, export, redaction).
- Ops: do retention numbers above look sane? Are our S3 size/IO estimates off?
- Security: recommend design for signatures (currently a placeholder). Should we accelerate KMS integration?

Quick links / references used while drafting:
- Slack: #private-deployments (thread: network-commit-proof)
- Prior doc: customer-network-handover-playbook-audit-scenarios.json (helps with handover UX)
- Ticket: JIRA-CORE-2345 (exporter schema)

Status: WIP. Expect follow-up with proto schema + console mockups next week.

-- Asha
